statements.impact_statement: glob() spends CPU time and memory in proportion to the pattern it is given; that is the POSIX behaviour glibc implements, not a defect in glibc. The CVE demonstrates the cost through an FTP daemon that passed remote STAT arguments to glob. Limiting pattern complexity is the job of the application that accepts untrusted patterns: Debian rates the CVE unimportant ('That's standard POSIX behaviour implemented by (e)glibc. Applications using glob need to impose limits for themselves') and no glibc change exists or is planned. An application that passes untrusted patterns to glob without limits is a finding against that application.
statements.status_notes: Versionless: glob's resource use on caller-supplied patterns is intended POSIX behaviour in every glibc version; no glibc fix exists or is planned.

statements.impact_statement: The CVE concerns the out-of-tree 'securelevel' patch series (Matthew Garrett's tree, commit d7a6be58edc0 "acpi: Disable APEI error injection if securelevel is set"): with securelevel set, APEI error injection through EINJ (einj_error_inject in drivers/acpi/apei/einj.c) stayed available. Ubuntu notes the CVE was assigned against an out-of-tree patch series. Mainline never had securelevel; its successor, kernel lockdown (Linux 5.4), restricts all of debugfs, through which EINJ is driven (commit 5496197f9b08 "debugfs: Restrict debugfs when the kernel is locked down"). nixpkgs' kernel carries no securelevel patches and is built without the lockdown LSM (CONFIG_SECURITY_LOCKDOWN_LSM is not set), so there is no securelevel or lockdown state for EINJ to bypass; EINJ in debugfs remains root-only by design.

statements.impact_statement: The stack protector's reference canary lives in the thread control block, which for threads sits at the top of the thread's stack, so a separate, already exploitable stack buffer overflow in a thread can also overwrite the reference value. This weakens a post-attack mitigation; it is not a flaw an attacker can trigger in glibc. Without another memory-corruption bug in an application there is nothing to bypass. glibc upstream treats it as a hardening request, not a security bug (sourceware bug 22850, open as an enhancement), and Debian rates it unimportant.
statements.status_notes: Versionless: upstream classifies this as hardening, not a vulnerability, in every glibc version; no fix exists.

statements.impact_statement: The attack needs a victim to run ldd on attacker-supplied ELF files whose segments overlap the loader; ldd then runs code from them. ldd works by loading the program through the dynamic loader and is not meant for untrusted binaries: glibc upstream says 'ldd is not intended to be executed on untrusted binaries, so this is not a security vulnerability' and that the loader assumes all binaries on disk are trusted (sourceware bug 22851). Nothing on NixOS runs ldd on files it receives; Debian rates the CVE unimportant.
statements.status_notes: Versionless: upstream does not treat ldd on untrusted binaries as a supported use in any glibc version; no fix exists.

statements.impact_statement: glibc reuses thread stacks and per-thread heaps from caches, which can make their addresses easier to predict. That only weakens ASLR as a defence; it gives an attacker nothing without a separate memory-corruption bug in an application. glibc upstream flags the report as a request for additional hardening, not a security bug (sourceware bug 22852), and Debian rates it unimportant. Where wanted, the thread stack cache can be turned off with the glibc.pthread.stack_cache_size=0 tunable (GLIBC_TUNABLES).
statements.status_notes: Versionless: upstream classifies this as hardening, not a vulnerability, in every glibc version; no fix exists.

statements.impact_statement: NVMe passthrough: the device can write more metadata than the user buffer. Since v6.2, passthrough I/O commands need no CAP_SYS_ADMIN, only a file descriptor on the namespace's device node (nvme_cmd_allowed() in drivers/nvme/host/ioctl.c); admin, vendor-specific and fabrics commands still require CAP_SYS_ADMIN. Unprivileged users cannot open those nodes: the generic character nodes /dev/ngXnY keep the kernel's root-only default (systemd's udev rules assign them no group or mode), and the block nodes belong to root:disk, a root-equivalent group. Upstream mitigated it for SGL-capable controllers in 6fad84a4d624 (v6.13, present in 6.18). Applies only while the nixos-vex condition nvme-nodes-privileged holds: a udev rule in services.udev.extraRules that mentions NVMe nodes removes this statement from the generated feed; rules shipped in services.udev.packages are not inspected. Source: https://cveawg.mitre.org/api/cve/CVE-2023-6238. nixpkgs ships Linux 6.18.54 at the pinned nixpkgs revision (c59305b).

statements.status_notes: ssh(1) client: '$' and '\' in a username given on the command line can inject shell syntax through ProxyCommand, Match exec and similar %-expansions. Fixed upstream in OpenSSH 10.6 (release notes: https://www.openssh.org/releasenotes.html); nixpkgs applies no fix to 10.5p1.

statements.action_statement: Update to OpenSSH 10.6 or later (nixpkgs has not packaged it at the pinned revision; candidate nixpkgs version bump). Until then, give certificate validity intervals in UTC (ssh-keygen -V with times ending in Z).
statements.status_notes: ssh-keygen(1): Daylight Saving Time is mishandled when converting dates, so certificates can get an expiry off by up to an hour. Fixed upstream in OpenSSH 10.6 (release notes: https://www.openssh.org/releasenotes.html); nixpkgs applies no fix to 10.5p1.

statements.action_statement: Update to OpenSSH 10.6 or later (nixpkgs has not packaged it at the pinned revision; candidate nixpkgs version bump). Until then, disable compression: services.openssh.settings.Compression = false; for sshd, and keep the client default (Compression no).
statements.status_notes: ssh(1), sshd(8): decompression does not check that inflated payloads stay within the maximum packet length. Fixed upstream in OpenSSH 10.6 (release notes: https://www.openssh.org/releasenotes.html); nixpkgs applies no fix to 10.5p1.

statements.action_statement: Update to OpenSSH 10.6 or later (nixpkgs has not packaged it at the pinned revision; candidate nixpkgs version bump). Until then, keep PermitTunnel at its default (no); NixOS does not set it.
statements.status_notes: sshd(8): the authorized_keys restrict keyword did not disable tunnel forwarding. Fixed upstream in OpenSSH 10.6 (release notes: https://www.openssh.org/releasenotes.html); nixpkgs applies no fix to 10.5p1.

statements.action_statement: Update to OpenSSH 10.6 or later (nixpkgs has not packaged it at the pinned revision; candidate nixpkgs version bump). Until then, do not override such options with none inside Match blocks in services.openssh.extraConfig.
statements.status_notes: sshd(8): some options documented to accept none (e.g. AuthorizedPrincipalsFile) treat it as a file name when set inside a Match block. Fixed upstream in OpenSSH 10.6 (release notes: https://www.openssh.org/releasenotes.html); nixpkgs applies no fix to 10.5p1.

statements.action_statement: Update to CPython 3.14.8 or later (nixpkgs has not packaged it at the pinned revision; candidate nixpkgs version bump).
statements.status_notes: ssl: use-after-free of a server-side SSLContext when an sni_callback switches SSLSocket.context and nothing else keeps the original context alive. The PSF CNA record bounds 3.14 as affected < 3.14.8; nixpkgs applies no fix to 3.14.7.
